transcript.content: Hello, what brings you in today?

Well, I... I guess what brings me in is that I can't keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like, I'll start talking about my overnight shift at the hospital, you know, because I work as an orderly, and then somehow I end up jumping to soccer. I used to play a lot of soccer back in high school. My jersey was this really bright blue, almost like the paint color they used in the new psych ward wing. Actually, speaking of the ward, the patient charts there are a mess right now, they changed the whole system and... wait, what was I saying? Right, my words. I just... I can see everyone getting lost when I talk. It's like my brain won't stay on the rails.
Have you been sleeping less than usual without feeling tired?

No, I... I definitely feel tired. Like, heavy tired. I try to sleep as much as I can, especially after my overnight shifts. The break room at the hospital has this awful couch, it's that fake leather that squeaks every time you move. One of the nurses, Brenda, she always leaves her magazines on it. Mostly cooking magazines. I tried making this lasagna recipe from one of them once, but I burnt the edges. My oven runs really hot, actually. The landlord said he’d fix it like three months ago, but he never did. He’s this older guy who drives a vintage Chevy, cherry red. You don't see cars in that exact shade much anymore, they're all just silver or black now... wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Sleep. Right. No, I don't have that thing where I don't need sleep. I'm pretty much always exhausted.
How long has it been difficult for you to keep your thoughts and words organized?

Well, I'd say it's been... about a year and a month now. Yeah, a year and a month. I remember because it was right around Halloween last year, and the hospital cafeteria had these pumpkin-shaped cookies. The frosting on them was way too hard, though, like, break-your-teeth hard. One of the other orderlies, Gary, he actually chipped a molar on one. He had to go to this dentist down on 4th street, the one with the big neon tooth sign in the window. That sign buzzes all night, it's so loud. You can hear it from blocks away if the wind is blowing the right direction. 

But anyway, that's when the disorganized stuff really started getting bad, my words getting all tangled up. And that’s also when the watching started. I started realizing that people were keeping tabs on me, you know, watching me. They put new security cameras in the ward right around then. They have these little red blinking lights. Red always means recording. I had a camcorder in high school with a red light, I used to film my soccer games with it. We actually made it to the state semi-finals my junior year, and we played on this artificial turf field that smelled exactly like hot tires... um, wait. Did I answer your question? About the time?
When these problems first began, were you using any drugs or substances besides prescribed medications?

No, I wasn't taking anything. I mean, I don't really do drugs or anything like that. I used to drink a little beer with the guys after our shifts sometimes, usually at this pub near the hospital called The Rusty Anchor. It has this huge, actual anchor right by the front door, painted black, but the paint is chipping off so you can see the rust underneath. They have these really good soft pretzels there, the kind with the big grains of salt on top. I always ask for extra mustard, the spicy brown kind, not the yellow stuff. The yellow stuff just tastes like vinegar to me. My mom used to put vinegar on our french fries when I was a kid. We went to this boardwalk in New Jersey once, and the seagulls there were so aggressive, they'd swoop right down and take a fry right out of your hand... wait, what did you ask me? About drugs? Yeah, no. Just... just the stuff the doctor gave me, nothing else.

final_diagnosis.reason: Persistent disorganized speech and persecutory delusional beliefs for approximately 13 months, without evidence of substance use or a manic episode, are most consistent with schizophrenia. The duration exceeds the minimum required for a schizophrenia-spectrum disorder.

confirmed_symptoms: Frequent derailment and rapid shifts between unrelated topics
Difficulty keeping thoughts and words organized
Conversation is difficult for others to follow
Repeatedly loses track of the question and intended topic
Belief that people are keeping tabs on or watching the patient
Interpretation of newly installed security cameras and blinking red lights as evidence of being monitored
Reports feeling tired and exhausted rather than unusually energetic
Denies drug use or other substances at symptom onset
Reports only occasional beer use and prescribed medications
